content.user_title: Design PostgreSQL Schemas With Best Practices
content.value_statement: PostgreSQL schema design can fail when data types, constraints, indexes, and migrations lack workload context. This skill turns entities, access patterns, and scale targets into PostgreSQL-specific design guidance.
actual_capabilities: Guides PostgreSQL table design using primary keys, constraints, and correct data types.
Recommends indexes for joins, filters, JSONB, arrays, and full-text search.
Explains partitioning, row-level security, generated columns, and common extensions.
Reviews migration risks such as concurrent indexes and volatile defaults.
Provides example patterns for users, orders, profiles, and JSONB attributes.
limitations: It does not connect to a database or inspect live query plans.
It focuses on PostgreSQL and is not a database-agnostic modeling guide.
It requires users to provide entities, access patterns, scale targets, and retention needs.
It does not replace migration testing, backups, or production change controls.

use_cases.title: Design a Feature Schema
use_cases.description: Plan tables, keys, constraints, and indexes for a new PostgreSQL feature before implementation starts.

use_cases.title: Review a Production Migration
use_cases.description: Check schema changes for locking, rewrite, indexing, and rollback risks before a release.

use_cases.title: Model Scalable Data Storage
use_cases.description: Choose JSONB, partitioning, RLS, and extension patterns for growing data products.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Basic Schema
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the PostgreSQL skill to design tables for this feature. Entities are [entities]. Common queries are [queries]. Expected scale is [scale].

prompt_templates.title: Review Data Types and Constraints
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this PostgreSQL table plan for data type, nullability, key, and constraint choices. Call out changes that improve correctness and maintainability.

prompt_templates.title: Plan Indexes for Workload
prompt_templates.prompt: Given these PostgreSQL queries and table sizes, recommend indexes and explain each tradeoff. Include composite, partial, expression, GIN, GiST, or BRIN options when useful.

prompt_templates.title: Audit an Advanced Migration
prompt_templates.prompt: Audit this PostgreSQL migration plan for locking, rewrites, data backfill, RLS, partitioning, and rollback risk. Suggest a safer deployment sequence.

output_examples.input: I need user and order tables with status tracking and reporting queries.
output: A normalized users table with a stable identity key and unique email handling.
An orders table with status checks, monetary precision, timestamps, and foreign key support.
Indexes for user lookups, created time reports, and safe parent row updates.

output_examples.input: Review my plan to store product attributes in JSONB.
output: Guidance on when JSONB is appropriate and when regular columns are safer.
Index choices for containment, key existence, scalar range filters, and generated columns.
Constraint ideas that keep flexible attributes within expected shapes.

output_examples.input: Plan a large event table with retention and tenant isolation.
output: A partitioning approach based on time and retention operations.
Row-level security considerations for tenant access control.
Index and migration advice that limits write overhead and release risk.

best_practices: Provide real access patterns, row counts, write rates, and retention needs before asking for design advice.
Validate generated schema ideas with migrations, staging data, and PostgreSQL query plans.
Prefer explicit constraints and indexes that match actual application behavior.
anti_patterns: Do not copy example tables without adapting names, constraints, and indexes to your workload.
Do not use JSONB as a replacement for core relational modeling.
Do not run destructive DDL in production without backups, tests, and rollback planning.

faq.question: Does this skill execute PostgreSQL commands?
faq.answer: No. It provides design guidance and examples. Users must run any database changes themselves.

faq.question: Can it tune live database queries?
faq.answer: It can suggest schema and index changes, but it does not inspect live databases or query plans.

faq.question: Is it useful for other databases?
faq.answer: It is PostgreSQL-specific. Some modeling ideas may transfer, but many recommendations use PostgreSQL features.

faq.question: Does it cover row-level security?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes guidance for enabling RLS and creating policies for row-level access control.

faq.question: Can it help with JSONB design?
faq.answer: Yes. It explains JSONB use, GIN indexes, scalar extraction, and constraints for flexible attributes.

faq.question: Should I apply its migration advice directly?
faq.answer: No. Review every migration with backups, staging tests, and production change controls.
